comments.author: @fredrika27
comments.text:
I lived in Nesland, Norway for some time back in the 80s. I loved it because there was a great work-life balance. I went to work at 8:00 and was home by 16:00. While there, I learned to knit and ski. I even tried the kiddie spring tower where kids train to jump from the 80m and 100m towers. What I remember so clearly was the number of girls learning to ski jump. Most of them did it for fun because at that time there was no international competition for women. Yet, the girls were very persistent and all took turns with the boys with some landing very well. As for me, I fell on my butt! However, my spill came after I landed and was not like the one we used to watch on ABC Wide World of Sports. I still got cheers for trying! 

What I miss: cutting wood every day for the cabin I stayed in! When you rent a cabin, wood is usually delivered uncut, in a pile before your door. One day, I decided I would cut enough wood for the entire week. Well after about 40 minutes I was winded, so I took my coat off in -5°C but kept on working. My landlord came out with his snow mobile pulling a mini wood splitter! He got off his snowmobile and said, "My wife and I had a bet that you'd never take off your jacket outside. I lost, so now I have to cut your wood!" Mind you I had two day woodpile that was stacked neatly. 

If my arms were not so tired, I'd given him a piece of my mind, but I need his excavator. Plus, he knew I was very prideful and wanted to be self-sufficient as the entire village had called us research scientists and engineers soft. I burst into laughter and we made quick work of the rest of the wood. When my husband got home and saw the woodpile, he took over a bottle of contraband that we were able to get past Norwegian customs. That bottle sat in pride of place for two years before it was opened for the couples 25 wedding anniversary!
